scope: Robot Hand and Quality Check Robot; original official builds, not invented extensions
pageConvention: One-based PDF page index; printed step number is separate. Manual pages do not have printed page numbers.
quantityPolicy: Quantities are transcribed from visually inspected numbered-step callouts. Joining an existing subassembly adds no new parts. Battery is part of the hub preparation and not a separately counted callout. Set storage-box illustrations are not robot inventory.
partIdPolicy: Stable local keys are descriptive research identifiers, not LEGO design/element IDs. Manufacturer partId remains null: no exact mold certification is claimed. geometryId is separately an LDraw DAT basename selected by contextual source-shape evidence in lego-part-crosswalk.json, not a manufacturer ID; resolve by input + build + key, especially azure-short-connector.

mechanism.dofStatus: Kinematic inference from single motor and coupled jaw linkage; not a manufacturer DOF specification
mechanism.description: Single-motor coupled two-jaw gripper, not an articulated multi-finger hand. Angled jaw links and the gray H-shaped rear coupler constrain the opening/closing motion.
mechanism.rangeReason: No dimensioned opening, mechanical joint-limit specification, or gripping-force figure in inspected manual/lesson. Official example drives motor by time/power, not a calibrated jaw opening.

operation.baseline: Lesson Building Tips describes opening/closing with left/right Hub buttons; current supplied SVG instead implements left-button press/release.
operation.inspectedProgram: F clockwise 0.2 s at startup; when left button pressed start F at -100% power; when left button released F clockwise 0.2 s.

Insert four black pins.
Join yellow base plate to frame/brackets.
Insert six base-plate pins.
Mount Color Sensor on plate.

Mount prepared yellow bricks beside Color Sensor.
Add two yellow curved tops.

Mount Hub upright on rear brackets and connect Color Sensor cable.

Make four loose sample packages from green, blue, red and magenta 2 x 4 bricks with three vertical axle holes, stacking two same-color bricks each; violet remains the lesson sensor enum, not the physical magenta material.

integration.description: Head is physically pinned onto the Idea Detector's yellow plate. The Idea Detector is not merely a separate suggested model. Four sample packages remain separate loose objects.

hierarchy.status: Physical sequence and members verified from imagery. Yaw/pitch and serial kinematics are engineering interpretation; exact coordinates, transforms, joint limits and numeric pin-hole indices are not supplied by these manuals.

quality-check.motorAxisPortMapping: A and F motor ports verified; assigning each port to an exact physical axis requires tracing cables or app model data and is not asserted here.

capabilities.colorSensor: RGB/HSV/LEGO color, reflected and ambient light; hardware can emit white light. Optimal color-reading distance 16 mm is a sensor specification, not a measured assembly clearance.
capabilities.distanceSensor: Ultrasonic 50–2000 mm, specified +/-20 mm; four independently addressable white eye-light segments. Installed in official head but the inspected lesson programs use eye-light output, not a distance-trigger condition.
capabilities.motors: Two medium angular motors with speed/position sensing, relative position and absolute +/-180-degree reporting. Reporting interval is not a mechanical travel limit.
capabilities.baseline: Initialize A+F at speed 75%, shortest path to position 0; play Cat Meow 1; light C eyes; alternate Hub display images ten times at 2 s each.
capabilities.possibleSolution: On D violet color, A clockwise 30 degrees, counterclockwise 60, clockwise 60, counterclockwise 30; Connect sound and Hub display.
capabilities.otherOfficialProgram: A+F speed 50%, shortest path to 350; red D triggers A 30/60/60/30-degree shake; green D triggers F 30/60/60/30-degree movement; sound/display actions also shown.
notDocumented: Distance-sensor inspection trigger in the inspected lesson program

assets.imageryInspection: All 32 hand, 16 Idea Detector and 20 Robot Head PDF pages visually inspected through local page renders/contact sheets; ambiguous linkage and cabling pages also opened individually.
assets.licenseFinding: LEGO Education legal notice allows non-commercial home personal download with notices intact; public/commercial copying or distribution requires written permission. No open redistribution license found for manuals or SVG imagery.
assets.cadFinding: No authorized complete CAD/MPD assembly located in searched sources. John Holbrook offers author-authorized educational-set parts palettes with attribution, not these assembled robots; this does not establish rights to LEGO manuals or third-party part geometry. OMR landing page inspected; not proof that no model exists anywhere.

geometryResolution.crosswalk: lego-part-crosswalk.json families and sourceCorrections, input hand-quality; resolve by input + build + key
geometryResolution.identifierRule: geometryId is an LDraw DAT basename, not a certified LEGO design/element ID; partId remains null. Source-shape selection does not certify historical mold or assembled transforms.
geometryResolution.resolvedShapes: Hand grips 15535 through-hole tiles; four-pin gray blocks 48989 provisional versus 65489; hand azure 60483 versus head azure 49283; head plain pin 3673; jaw and sample bricks 39789 vertical-axlehole family.

gaps: Official numeric design/element IDs remain unresolved; local labels must not be presented as manufacturer IDs.
No authoritative complete CAD/MPD assembly or exact assembled transforms verified.
No calibrated hand opening, force, full joint travel or pin-index coordinate table documented.
Hand lesson prose mentions left/right buttons, whereas current program imagery uses left-button press/release; preserve provenance rather than silently harmonizing.
Quality Check motor A/F physical axis mapping not independently traced.
Lesson embedded videos were not downloaded or frame-inspected; behavioral claims above come from inspected official prose and program imagery, not a claimed video observation.
